Welcome
Mrs Sara Watkins, Headteacher
Welcome to our kind and caring Church of England school set in the wonderful surroundings of the village of Charlton Horethorne.
Recently described by a visitor as ‘small but perfectly formed,’ our school has mixed age classes with children from the Foundation Stage to Year 6. We are very proud of our Christian values and use these at the heart of everything we do to ensure all our children
LEARN, ENJOY, ACHIEVE and FLOURISH!

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Values and Spirituality | Charlton Horethorne CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision, Values and Spirituality
Theological Roots Learning together in friendship and faith…
‘Life in all its fullness’ John 10:10
The phrase ‘life in all its fullness’ comes from the Bible, specifically from the book of John chapter 10 verse 10, in which Jesus says, “I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.” This is Jesus calling us to a full life in mind, body, heart and spirit.
At Charlton Horethorne Primary School we understand that life can be full of WOW and OW moments: the awe and wonder moments where your heart and soul sing, you feel blessed, you gasp with excitement or feel truly happy and also the moments where we are brought up short, when we are shocked or saddened or surprised. We believe the purpose of education is to nurture and enable every child to thrive and to be the person they are fully capable of being.
Our school is a special place where we value every child as unique and we strive to develop them academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually in our happy and nurturing environment.
SPIRITUALITY in Charlton Horethorne
As a church school, spirituality is very important to us and is a journey where we explore who we are, our relationships with one another, our community, the world around us and beyond. We use Windows, Mirrors, Doors to help children understand the fundamental concepts of spirituality: looking out, looking in and looking ahead whilst we learn from, reflect on and respond to our experiences.
We know the development of spirituality can have a beneficial influence on a child’s well-being and their mental health and we aim to create an environment that will nurture people’s minds, body and soul. However, we acknowledge it is a deeply personal journey.
Please take a moment to read our latest SIAMS report from June 2025
Together we give our children an environment where they can LEARN, ENJOY, ACHIEVE and FLOURISH.
‘He’s the good shepherd…everywhere I go he knows’
COLLECTIVE WORSHIP and OUR VALUES
Our values are important to us as we live and learn together in our school. We have 12 in total, and are on a two year rolling programme incorporating the values as set out in the Collective Worship resource ‘Imaginor: Roots and Fruits.’ There are 6 values per year, one each half term and these remind us how to live and learn successfully together, in a caring environment that allows us all to flourish.
We also have Daniel England from Daniel England Ministries (DEM) visiting us each half term bringing his wonderful worship experience: songs, Bible stories, his guitar and always fun and laughter. ” Sharing God’s love with all those we meet” https://dem.org.uk
Our 12 Values
Year A:
Generosity
‘Love thy neighbour as yourself.’ (Mark 12.31)
“The person who gives with a smile is the best giver because God loves a cheerful giver.” Mother Teresa
Being generous is a conscious decision from the heart to do something with what you have. Christians believe that God calls his people to be generous with what he has given to them. It is a sign of trust in God, that there will be enough for everyone, so share it. Being generous isn’t always about money, we can be generous in so many other practical ways.
Compassion (Love)
‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind and, Love your neighbour as yourself.’ (Luke 10. 27)
‘Compassion’ and ‘sympathy’ have much in common and both are stronger in meaning than simply ‘feeling sorry for’ someone. The words have their roots in the idea of ‘suffering with’ someone, putting yourself in someone else’s shoes and experiencing what they experience. This leads to a desire to act, to do something. It is not about ‘doing good’ from a position of strength or ‘remembering those less fortunate than ourselves.’ Compassion requires an act of imagination and humility to share in the lives of others.
Courage
Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.’
Courage is often about continuing to do what you would normally do even when faced with extraordinary situations. Many Christians believe that God asks us to offer our skills, talents and abilities in the face of adversity, and that he will use that courageousness to achieve great things. The word ‘courage’ comes from the Latin word ‘cor’ = heart.
Forgiveness
‘Forgive us our sins, as we also forgive everyone who sins against us.’ (Luke 11.4)
Forgiveness is fundamental to the character of God. Throughout the Bible, God is described as slow to anger, abounding in love and forgiving sin (Numbers 14:18). Forgiveness cannot be given or received unless it is asked for, and the asking must be genuine and from the heart. Too often ‘sorry’ is said very easily, implying: ‘All I need to do is say I’m sorry and everything will be OK’. Real repentance demands that we take what we have done wrong with the utmost seriousness and have a deep desire not to do it again.
Friendship
‘A friend is always loyal, and a brother is born to help in time of need.’ (Proverbs 17.17)
Friends are incredibly important as children grow up. As part of this value we consider how to be a good friend and how to encourage each other. Friendship is a key concept in the Christian framework with Jesus being criticised for being a ‘friend of sinners’.
Jesus tells stories about a heavenly banquet to which all are invited. The barriers between people are broken down in a loving community based around God.
True friendship allows each person to grow, to become themselves. This ensures that the unique individuality of each person is recognised, echoing the value placed by God on the preciousness of each person.
Respect
‘Do to others as you would have them do to you’ (Matthew 7.12)
Respect is readiness to listen/Everyone being valued/Showing appreciation/Praying for people/Expressing opinions sensitively/Caring for our environment/ Treating property carefully
Christians believe that each person is unique and everyone is special to God. It is important to respect and value difference. When St Peter was writing a letter to his friends who were going through difficult times he said ‘Show proper respect to everyone’ (1 Peter 2.17)
Year B
Thankfulness
‘Always be thankful.’ (1 Thessolonians 5.16)
Thankfulness and praise are at the heart of Christian worship. Thankfulness is directed at God who gives and sustains life. Seeing the world as God’s creation underpins the way we approach everything in life; seeing it as a gift. Paul frequently encourages us to ‘be thankful’ and says that our lives should ‘overflow with thankfulness’. “Give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.” Thessalonians 5:18
Trust
‘My God is my strength in whom I trust.’ (Psalm 18.2)
Trust is the very essence of faith; trust in the God who is trustworthy. Trust is essential to human life and lies at the heart of all relationships. Trust entails vulnerability, putting yourself in others’ hands. We have to trust experts – pilots, dentists, surgeons. Yet, within our society, there often seems to be mutual distrust between people and those responsible for governing them.
Perseverance
I call do all things through Him who strengthens me’ ( Philippians 4.13)
Emphasis upon endurance is common in the New Testament where it is linked with patience and suffering. St Paul is certain that endurance is honed by suffering, is character building and is characterised by love (Romans 5:3-4; I Corinthians 4:12 – 13). It is linked with self-control, godliness (2 Peter 1:6) and steadfastness.
At its root, endurance is recognition that life is sometimes difficult and painful, and that it is important not to give up in the face of adversity. Endurance and perseverance are only possible where there is hope and that hope is based on the enduring nature of God’s love and faithfulness. Even Jesus, for all his strength and ability to endure, looked to his disciples to help and sustain him by watching and praying with him (Matthew 26).
Justice
‘What does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God’ (Micah 6.8)
Justice is not about a culture which encourages everyone to insist on their own rights at the expense of others. It is about a community that knows that everyone’s well-being is bound up with that of everyone else.
A commitment to justice leads to fierce opposition to injustice in whatever form it may be found. Justice means giving all people – particularly the poor and oppressed – what it is right and fair for them to have: life, health, freedom and dignity. It is about acting out of a concern for what is right and seeing right prevail. It is about social justice, especially for those who suffer most and are least able to protect themselves.
Service
‘Serve one another in love.’ (Galatians 5.13)
Words relating to ‘servant’ and ‘service’ are central in Christian theology. Some of the most important prophecies in Isaiah speak of the coming of the ‘Servant of the Lord’ and his role as a ‘suffering servant.’ That is why Jesus said that he ‘came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.’
Jesus washed the feet of his disciples at the Last Supper. This turned upside down the normal relationship between master and disciple, leader and follower. In many ways, this astonishing action symbolizes the essence of the Incarnation: God stooping to share the human condition. Jesus is very clear about the meaning of his action: ‘Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet. I have set you an example that you should do as I have done.’
Truth and Truthfulness
‘Tell the truth to each other’ (Zechariah 8.16)
‘God wants us to grow up, to know the whole truth and tell it in love—like Christ in everything. We take our lead from Christ, who is the source of everything we do’ (Ephesians 4.15)
Truth is such an important element of life and sometimes we need courage to be honest. In our worship and our discussions we ask big questions about why it can difficult for us to face the truth, to admit the truth or to even recognise what is true. We also ask what it means to be true to oneself!
Our Values
Autumn 1– Generosity Autumn 2– Compassion Spring 1– Courage Spring 2– Forgiveness Summer 1– Friendship Summer 2– Respect
Autumn 1-Thankfulness Autumn 2– Trust Spring 1– Perseverance Spring 2– Justice Summer 1– Service Summer 2– Truthfulness
Our School Prayer and Blessing
Lord, bless our school That working together and playing together We may learn to serve you And to serve each other. Amen
May God, who is the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, bless us. Amen

pageCache.text:
About Us
Charlton Horethorne is a small, rural school at the heart of the local community in a beautiful Somerset village where we learn together in friendship and faith to give us ‘life in all its fullness’ John 10:10
We have three classes; Ladybird: EYFS and Year 1; Bee: Years 2, 3,and 4 and Dragonfly Years 5 and 6. Our classes are led by experienced teachers who are supported by skilful teaching assistants to support all children with their learning.
In our school we believe that every child is special and our pupils are valued and nurtured by hardworking, caring and dedicated staff. We believe that children learn best when they are happy and stimulated to learn. The school prides itself on supporting all children in the classroom and on providing opportunities for children to take part in a range of out of school activities. We run various sports clubs throughout the year and participate in local sports competitions. In addition the children have the opportunity to join our after school enrichment clubs. We undertake a number of visits during the school year including a residential visit for Year 5 and 6 to Kilve activity centre where children can experience a series of adventurous activities and have great fun!
Everything we do is underpinned by our Christian vision and values, which creates a very caring, supportive environment. We have a well-earned reputation for being a “family” school where every child is treated with respect and encouraged to value themselves and those around them.

Governance
2026-2027
Local Governing Committees
The Local Governing Committee (LGC/Governors) support the Trustees to fulfil their responsibility for oversight of each school within the Trust, acting as the eyes and ears of the Board at local level. Their role is more focused than that of a traditional school governing body. The SAST central team manages – finance, HR, Estates, IT, and others.
The responsibility of the LGC is to monitor and scrutinise School Improvement, SEND (including Pupil Premium and other disadvantaged pupils), Safeguarding and Community Relationships. The LGC provides challenge and support to the Headteacher and senior leadership team, and represent the Trust to local stakeholders – parents, students, staff and the community. Governors are are elected from among that school’s parents, while a further governor will be elected by the staff. The Headteacher is ex officio. The remaining governors are appointed by the Trustees following recommendation from the LGC and Headteacher, based on skills and experience, or in our Church of England academies, the Diocese of Salisbury and the Diocese of Bath & Wells receive and consider nominations and appoint. Ex ‘VA’ schools must have a majority of foundation governors and ex ‘VC’ 25% of governors must be foundation. Each governor is appointed for a term of four years, after which time, with agreement from the Diocese or Trustees, they may agree to renewal of further term(s).
The LGC will meet at the beginning of each full term (three times a year), plus an additional meeting to review published exam performance. Typically, this additional meeting will take place during the summer term for primary schools, once the SATS results have been published, whereas for secondary schools, this meeting will take place during the autumn term

Charlton Horethorne is a small rural school at the heart of the local community.
Our mixed class structure means we have flexibility when it comes to admissions. It is not expected that any parents who have expressed a preference will be refused admission to Charlton Horethorne for their son or daughter.
If you would like to come and visit our school please contact the school office who will be happy to arrange this for you. If you would like to apply for a place at our school. Please visit the Somerset website and click on the link below.

FSA
Friends of the School Association (FSA)
As a parent of a child at Charlton Horethorne Primary we are ALL members of the FSA, and you are very welcome to take part in whatever way you are able. The FSA is open to ALL parents, carers, staff and friends of the school.
The FSA is a registered charity, constituted separately from the school. Our primary aim is to raise funds and support activities to enhance the experience and education of the children in our school. For example, Christmas activities in school, transport for school trips, special items for the classrooms or playground. We also aim to encourage the sense of community and belonging within our school through the activities we organise and support. Hopefully you will find the more you get involved with the FSA the more friendships you will make and the more a part of the school community you will feel.
The FSA has a committee elected annually in the Autumn term. The committee is:
Kristina Ackland: Treasurer
Scarlett Wills: Secretary
As a committee our role is to facilitate the activity of the FSA, not to organise everything! So we welcome ideas, suggestions and offers of help at any time. We hold meetings at least once a term, and circulate the minutes to all parents via the school office. The FSA try to keep parents well informed of forthcoming events and activities through flyers, posters, school newsletters and this website. We also have an FSA email group to communicate ideas and requests for help in between meetings. If you would like to be added to this please let the school office know your details for the attention of Rachel.
As a registered charity, we are keen to benefit from any existing fundraising schemes. Here are a few we are signed up with, and if you know of any more please tell us:
Pink & Greene (greetings cards) www.pinkandgreene.com
Recycle 4 Charity (recycle your inkjet cartridges). Please ask the school office for the recycling envelopes.
Easyfundraising (raise money for your chosen charity when you shop online). Sign up at this link, it is easy and we have raised over £200 already! www.easyfundraising.org.uk/invite/6CNXW5/

pageCache.text:
SAST
Our Mission
On the 1st May 2019 Charlton Horethorne Primary School become an academy and joined the SAST (Schools Achieving Success Together). The school became the first primary school in Somerset to join SAST.
The SAST was formed in June 2017, and has now grown to include 18 schools across North and West Dorset and South Somerset. We currently have around 5,000 students and we employ over 850 staff.
Our Vision
Flourishing children
At the heart of the vision are the children. SAST is dedicated to helping every child flourish —academically, emotionally, and socially. This involves fostering a supportive, inclusive environment where students feel safe, encouraged, and inspired to grow. By focusing on individual strengths, talents, and wellbeing, we aim to develop confident, capable young people who are prepared for the challenges and opportunities of life.
Flourishing schools are learning communities. SAST recognises that strong, dynamic schools are essential for effective learning. We want our schools to be vibrant educational environments where leaders, teachers, and support staff, work collaboratively to deliver excellent outcomes. Through innovative teaching practices, continuous professional development, and a focus on wellbeing, SAST schools aim to be beacons of educational excellence, offering a holistic experience that goes beyond the classroom.
Flourishing children
SAST believes that schools are at the heart of their communities. When schools thrive, so do the neighbourhoods and families around them. The “Flourishing Communities” aspect of our mission emphasises the role of schools as hubs of local life, fostering strong relationships with parents, local organisations, and businesses. By engaging with and contributing to the community, SAST hopes to create a cycle of positive impact, where education not only benefits individuals but strengthens the community.
Together, these three pillars encapsulate SAST’s commitment to creating an environment where everyone can flourish in harmony.
Our Values
Partnership Our family of schools believe that partnership is key to success. By working together with students, parents, staff, and the wider community, we foster an environment where all voices are valued. Through shared goals and mutual respect, we create opportunities for growth and achievement, ensuring that together, we can build a brighter future for everyone.
Equity We are committed to providing every student with the resources, opportunities, and support they need to succeed, regardless of their background or circumstances. For us, equity means more than fairness; it is about creating an inclusive environment where all individuals can flourish. We strive to remove barriers to learning, ensuring that every student is empowered to reach their full potential.
Aspiration We encourage every student to dream big and aim high, nurturing their ambitions and helping them to realise their goals. Through high-quality education and a supportive environment, we promote a culture where every individual is encouraged to grow and flourish. We equip our students with the skills and confidence to explore new possibilities and make a meaningful impact in the world.
Kaizen Inspired by the philosophy of continuous improvement; kaizen reflects our commitment to always striving for better. At SAST, we believe that growth is a constant journey. We encourage students, staff, and the wider community to embrace challenges, reflect on experiences, and seek out opportunities for learning and improvement. Through innovation and perseverance, we create a dynamic environment where progress is celebrated, and excellence is a daily pursuit.
